pages.title: ACT CRM proposal
pages.intro: One workspace for the job, its documents and the next step.
paragraphs: ACT needs a request to move from the website through quoting, signing, payment and assessment without staff repeatedly re-entering details or checking separate systems to find out what happens next.

We propose completing a CRM around that workflow. Jotform, Microsoft 365, DocuSign and Xero keep their roles. The CRM connects the handovers and gives the team a clear record of each enquiry, proposal and project.
rows: The outcome
Staff can see the job history, who owns the next task, which documents are current and what is waiting on the client.
The first release
A representative ACT request through proposal approval, signing, invoice and payment, followed by assessment and inspection tasks.
The decision
Agree the first-release workflow, remaining ACT inputs, acceptance tests and commercial terms.
pages.note: Discussion draft based on ACT's 9 October walkthrough and retained project records. Final scope and commercial terms require agreement.

pages.title: What needs to change
pages.intro: The extra work sits between the steps ACT already follows.
rows: What ACT described
What that means for the team
Jotform emails a request, then staff type the details into BCS.
The same information is handled twice before quoting begins.
Pricing, Word proposals, appointment forms, signatures and invoices span separate tools.
Staff have to carry the job forward and check which step is complete.
Files need consistent names, categories and approved or superseded status.
The team needs to know which document to use without searching through versions.
Tasks, inspection bookings and reporting need a shared view.
Owners need to see workloads, unresolved actions and which jobs are ready to progress.
paragraphs: The first priority is to connect these handovers while keeping ACT staff in control of fees, proposal content and certification decisions.

pages.title: The proposed change
pages.intro: Keep the tools that work. Make the progress of each job visible.
rows: Current handover
Proposed ACT workflow
Request email followed by manual setup.
An in-scope Jotform submission creates one enquiry with its contacts, uploaded plans and a review task.
Proposal preparation across Word documents and pricing files.
Staff select the approved template and fee lines, review the proposal and prepare the required forms.
Signing, invoicing and payment checked separately.
Signed documents return to the record. The agreed Xero workflow records invoice and payment status separately.
Assessment and inspections require further coordination.
Tasks follow the approved payment rule. Bookings, reminders and exceptions are visible against the job.
paragraphs: Enquiries that do not convert remain available for reporting. An accepted proposal and a paid invoice remain distinct events. The BCS transition is agreed before any cutover.

pages.title: What the ACT team gets
pages.intro: A workspace built around certification work, rather than a generic sales pipeline.
rows: Part of the CRM
What staff can do
Enquiries, proposals and projects
Track each stage separately, retain the history and assign the responsible staff member.
Proposal and document workspace
Use ACT templates and approved fee schedules. Review draft proposals, manage related forms and distinguish approved documents from superseded versions.
Tasks and inspections
Assign work, see workloads, use approved checklists and manage inspection requests with the retained Microsoft calendar.
Communications and reporting
Keep relevant mail and SMS activity with the job. Define reporting from ACT's tracking spreadsheet before building the final reports.
AI assistance
Suggest a proposal template from job details for staff to accept or override. AI does not set fees or make certification decisions.
pages.note: The release scope includes only the agreed templates, forms, roles and workflows. Additional reporting or migration work is scoped separately.

pages.title: Follow one ACT job through it
pages.intro: An illustrative walkthrough of the workflow discussed with ACT.
rows: 1. Request and review
A customer submits a Jotform request with plans. The CRM records the enquiry and assigns the quoting review.
2. Prepare the proposal
Staff check the work type, fee and template, then review the proposal and required appointment documentation.
3. Obtain signatures
The approved package goes through DocuSign. Completed documents return to the correct record; incomplete signing remains visible.
4. Invoice and payment
The agreed Xero invoice is created once. Assessment starts only at the payment milestone ACT approves, including any staged-payment exceptions.
5. Assessment and inspection
The job has an owner, checklist and documents. Microsoft calendar bookings trigger agreed confirmations and reminders; unclear replies create a staff task.
pages.note: This page explains the proposed sequence. Live ACT account tests will confirm each connection before launch.

pages.title: The scope we need to agree
pages.intro: These decisions let us complete and test the first workflow correctly.
rows: Scope item
ACT decision or input
Forms, templates and prices
Confirm the active ACT/NSW request forms, approved Word templates, fee schedule and required signers.
Staff and records
Confirm roles, financial visibility, quoting ownership, project assignment and unique references.
Documents and checklists
Approve categories, standard names, approved/superseded rules and the checklist versions to use.
Invoicing and bookings
Confirm invoice types, the initial upfront-payment rule and any 60/40 exceptions. Confirm inspection calendar, sender, reminders and reply routing.
Reporting and transition
Supply the tracking spreadsheet and agree the first reports. Define whether historical BCS records move, what moves and how the existing process stays available.
paragraphs: We will use ACT's authorised Jotform, Microsoft 365, DocuSign, Xero and Twilio accounts. Account identities, access and required plans are checked before integration testing.

pages.title: The business case
pages.intro: Measure the repeated work the CRM is intended to remove.
rows: Area
How ACT can measure the change
Request entry
Compare staff minutes spent entering each eligible request before and after the form connection.
Proposal preparation
Measure time to prepare, review and send a proposal using the approved templates and prices.
Signing and payment checks
Record manual follow-ups and time spent checking document, invoice and payment status.
Documents and inspections
Measure time finding current files and handling booking changes, reminders and exceptions.
Overall cost
Compare measured benefit with build, support, usage and any additional software costs. Count existing licences only where costs actually change.
paragraphs: No annual savings figure has been assumed. ACT and the delivery team will agree a baseline and review period. Time released is staff capacity unless an actual expense is removed.
pages.note: Extra jobs and additional revenue should only enter the case when ACT confirms demand, capacity and how the system contributes.

pages.title: How we will deliver it
pages.intro: Complete the existing work, connect ACT's accounts and test the full handover.
rows: Stage
Work and approval
1. Confirm ACT's rules
Agree first-release scope, templates, pricing, roles, payment exceptions, calendars and document rules.
2. Complete the workspace
Review the retained project, proposal, forms and inspection screens with ACT. Resolve the gaps against the agreed scope.
3. Prove the connections
Use controlled submissions, signers and recipients to test Jotform, Microsoft 365, DocuSign, Xero and Twilio through one representative job.
4. Train and launch
ACT runs the agreed user tests. Resolve defects, provide the operating guide and approve the cutover before live work moves.
paragraphs: Target dates and delivery owners will be agreed after access and the first-release scope are confirmed. Earlier test targets are not a new launch commitment.
pages.note: Retained build evidence includes proposal editing, saved revisions, supplied forms and DocuSign sandbox tests. It does not replace ACT production-account acceptance.

pages.title: Handover and next steps
pages.intro: ACT should accept a working workflow, with clear ownership and support.
rows: Acceptance tests
One enquiry and task per submission; correct files and proposal; signed documents linked to the job; one correct invoice; payment-driven task handover; bookings and replies handled correctly.
Access and exceptions
Test staff roles and finance visibility. Check failed connections, duplicate events, missing files and cancelled bookings so staff can see and recover the work.
Handover and support
Provide admin access, training and documentation. Agree support contact, response expectations, export/backup arrangements and ownership terms in the final agreement.
Changes and cutover
Approve additional work and costs before building it. Agree the BCS/historical-data boundary and recovery plan before switching day-to-day work.
paragraphs: Next: Alex and Scott confirm the workflow and remaining inputs; we agree the first-release scope, commercial terms and dates; then the team completes the controlled ACT acceptance run.
pages.note: Client legal entity and contracting details will be confirmed on the final agreement.
